Full job description

About HK 24-BPO



HK 24-BPO is a fast-growing customer service outsourcing company serving cross-border e-commerce brands. We partner with Amazon and Shopify sellers across smart electronics, smart home, wearables, and audio product categories. Backed by our proprietary AI + human customer service system, we deliver reliable, high-quality support to customers around the world. We are now expanding our team and looking for a dedicated HR Specialist to join us in Clark.



About the Job



We are hiring an office-based HR Specialist in Clark, Pampanga. This is not a remote position — you will work from our office and play a key role in managing the full recruitment cycle and daily HR operations for our growing customer service team.



What You'll Do:



- Source, screen, and recruit customer service representatives across multiple channels (OnlineJobs.ph, referrals, social media, etc.)

- Manage the end-to-end hiring process — from posting job ads to scheduling interviews and onboarding new hires

- Maintain employee records, attendance tracking, and performance documentation

- Handle day-to-day HR administrative tasks and employee relations

- Coordinate with the management team in China to align hiring priorities and timelines

- Support training coordination and new hire orientation

- Build and maintain a talent pipeline for ongoing hiring needs

- 1–2 years of experience in HR, recruitment, or talent acquisition

- Experience hiring for customer service or BPO roles is a strong plus

- Excellent communication skills in English, both written and verbal

- Highly organized with strong attention to detail

- Comfortable working with spreadsheets, job boards, and communication tools

- Self-driven and able to work independently in a fast-paced environment

- Based in or willing to relocate to Clark, Pampanga

What We Offer:



- Competitive salary: $500 – $600 per month

- Office-based position in Clark — stable, professional work environment

- Clear career growth path — grow into a senior HR role as the team scales

- Be part of a tech-driven company that combines AI with human expertise

- Hands-on experience building a team from the ground up

title: Long-Term Video Editor Needed — Funny Vlog-Style Storytelling (CapCut)
description:
Looking for a long-term editor to work on lifestyle/personal brand content across Instagram Reels, TikTok, and Snapchat. This is an ongoing contract, not a one-off. I need someone reliable I can build a consistent workflow with.



**Style:**

- Funny vlog-style storytelling — edits should feel like a narrative/story unfolding, not just quick clips strung together

- Fast cuts, high energy, trending-sound driven

- Comedic zooms/punches for emphasis (think meme-style editing, not corporate)

- Strong sense of pacing and timing — you know when a joke needs a beat vs. a quick cut, and how to build a story arc within a short-form video

- Comfortable with pacing similar to voiceover/talking-head (cutting dead air, tightening rambles into a punchy story)



**Requirements:**

- Must be fluent in CapCut

- Portfolio/reel showing this exact editing style — funny, story-driven vlogs (not just "professional" editing, and not just meme clips — I want to see storytelling with comedic timing)

- Fast turnaround (raw footage to finished edit)

- Available for regular ongoing volume (ex., 3-5 videos/week)

- Open to per-video rate or monthly retainer



**To apply, please send:**

1. 2-3 sample edits that show funny, story-driven vlog editing specifically (not just meme clips or quick-cut compilations — I want to see how you take raw talking/vlog footage and turn it into a tight, entertaining story)

2. Your rate (per video or weekly/monthly retainer)

3. Typical turnaround time

4. Availability for long-term work



Looking to start with a paid trial period before committing to an ongoing rate. Thank you!!

title: FULL-TIME VIDEO EDITOR
description:
The role

You are the person who takes raw footage and turns it into scroll-stopping content. Every day, you will receive raw video clips from our shop floor (printing presses running, orders being made, finished products) and talking-head recordings from the owner. Your job is to edit these into short-form and long-form videos optimized for each platform.



This is a high-volume role. You will produce 8–15 edited video pieces per day across different formats. Speed, consistency, and understanding of what makes content perform on social media are essential.



What you will do

Short-form video editing (primary focus — 70% of time)

• Edit raw clips into 15–60 second videos for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts

• Add captions/subtitles to all videos (burned-in, styled, readable)

• Write and add text hooks in the first 1–2 seconds of every video

• Add transitions, zoom effects, and pacing that match platform trends

• Select and sync trending audio/music where appropriate

• Create satisfying loop videos from production process footage (press pulls, ink shots, transfer peels)

• Edit before/after reveal videos with dramatic transitions

• Format and resize the same video for different platforms (9:16, 1:1, 16:9)



Long-form video editing (20% of time)

• Edit 1 long-form YouTube video per week (5–15 minutes)

• Full process walkthroughs: a single order from design to shipping

• Educational content: print method comparisons, branding guides, industry tips

• Add intro/outro, lower thirds, chapter markers, and b-roll where needed

• Create compelling thumbnails for YouTube videos



Ad creative (10% of time)

• Edit short video ads for Meta 
/Instagram) campaigns

• Create multiple variations of the same ad for A/B testing

title: YouTube Channel Manager — Faceless Channels — Freelance, Remote
description:
I run a portfolio of faceless YouTube channels from the Netherlands with a remote team of scriptwriters, video editors and thumbnail artists. I'm looking for one person to become my right hand on the operational side.



Start date, hours and salary



Starting 1 October 2026. You begin at around 12 hours a week while you learn the channel and the pipeline. As you take on more — and as we add channels — that grows toward full-time, up to 40 hours a week. How fast depends on you. Pay is negotiable, and grows as your responsibilities do.



How this grows



You start with one channel — BloopUniverse, in the celebrity bloopers and compilations niche — and you run it end to end. Once it's running smoothly, we add a second channel built on AI scripts and voiceover. Then a third, and so on. The portfolio is expanding, and I need someone who grows with it rather than someone I have to replace when it does. Your rate goes up as the scope does.



So the first months are about BloopUniverse, done properly. The long game is that you manage several channels, each with its own team.



Working with AI is a requirement, not a bonus



Read this part carefully, because it's the core of the job.



For my other channels I've built AI agents that produce first drafts of scripts and thumbnail concepts. You paste in the title and references, and the agent gives you something back. That part is easy. What I'm hiring for is everything after: judging what came out, rewriting it, sharpening it, and rejecting it when it isn't good enough.



Daily work with Claude and ChatGPT is non-negotiable. If you're not already using these tools every day and getting real results out of them, this role isn't for you. But if you know why one prompt lands and another doesn't, and you can spot mediocre AI output in three seconds, you'll do well here.



Week to week



Brief and chase our scriptwriters, editors and thumbnail artists — deadlines, feedback, revisions

Upload and schedule: titles, descriptions, tags, thumbnails, end screens, playlists

Keep the content calendar current so nobody is waiting on anyone

Report weekly on views, CTR and retention — and tell me what you think it means

Write and publish community posts

Run the AI agents for scripts and thumbnails, then rewrite, sharpen and reject until the output is genuinely good (at a later stage)

And more — curious? Ask me for the full task list



I pick the topics. You own everything from there to published, with my input whenever you need it.



What I'm looking for



Creative judgment. You can read a script and know which joke doesn't land. You can look at a thumbnail and know why nobody would click it.

Strong communication skills — clear, prompt, and proactive

Experience managing and directing freelancers

Excellent written English — you'll be rewriting scripts, not proofreading them

Hands-on YouTube Studio experience

You fix things without being asked. If something in the pipeline is broken, I want your solution, not just the problem.

At least 4 hours of overlap with Central European Time

Daily, fluent use of Claude and ChatGPT (required — see above)



Nice to have



Experience with faceless or compilation channels

Experience coordinating freelancers

You find this stuff funny. If celebrity bloopers make you laugh, you'll be better at this than someone who doesn't care.



Terms



Freelance contractor, paid monthly. You invoice me; you handle your own taxes.

Rate is negotiable — tell me what you're looking for and we'll discuss it. I pay for judgment, not for hours logged.

Flexible hours. Deadlines matter, the clock doesn't.

Real ownership. You run the channel; I'm not looking over your shoulder daily.



How to apply



Start your application with the word BLOOPERS, followed by the best way to reach you directly. Anything without it gets deleted unread.



Then, briefly:



Tell me about a YouTube channel you've worked on and what you did. Link it if you can — if you can't share it, describe the channel and the numbers instead.

Pick any faceless compilation channel on YouTube. One thing they do well, one thing you'd change. Two sentences each.

Which AI tools do you use daily, and what for? Be specific.

Describe one time you used AI for creative work and the output wasn't good enough. What did you do?

title: Operations Manager
description:
The Operations Manager runs the operational backbone of the business and acts as the Management Representative for our Integrated Management System. You will keep day-to-day operations running smoothly and compliantly — procurement, supplier, asset and access management, business continuity, document control and cross-department coordination across our UK and Philippines teams — while owning the QMS, ISMS and AIMS: maintaining them, keeping them audit-ready, running internal audits and management reviews, and driving continual improvement. You will also run the quarterly project cadence that keeps every department's projects on track. It is a hands-on governance and operations leadership role reporting directly to the Managing Director, with scope to build an Operations Assistant function and automate recurring work.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Integrated Management System & governance (Management Representative)

• Establish, maintain and continually improve the IMS across ISO 9001, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001, and report its performance to top management.

• Own the internal audit programme end-to-end — plan, schedule, conduct or coordinate audits, log findings and drive them to closure; act as primary liaison with BSI and external/certification auditors.

• Organise and facilitate management reviews; capture minutes, decisions and actions.

• Run document control: the controlled-document register, version control, scheduled reviews and approvals.

• Coordinate nonconformity and corrective/preventive action (NC/CAPA) across all three systems, tracking each to closure.

• Own the integrated risk & opportunity process: maintain the register, facilitate assessments,

drive treatments and recommend residual-risk acceptance to the Managing Director.

• Steward the scope, Statement of Applicability, policies and objectives, keeping them current.



Project & portfolio governance

• Run the quarterly project cadence across the business — review each department's projects to ensure they are running as planned, on scope and on schedule.

• Maintain the project tracker; surface slippage, risks, blockers and dependencies, and hold owners to their commitments.

• Report project status and portfolio health to the Managing Director, and keep BAU (run) work and project (change) work clearly separated.



Compliance, information security & risk

• Administer information-security operations: asset inventory, access identities and periodic user-access reviews, supplier/third-party security management, BYOD compliance, i
 logging and coordination, and change management.

• Maintain the legal, regulatory and contractual requirements register and coordinate operational compliance (UK GDPR/data protection, sector and AI-governance obligations).

• Own business-continuity and disaster-recovery readiness — plans, drills and tests.



Operations & resource management

• Run the procurement and purchasing process, including supplier onboarding and due diligence.

• Coordinate cross-department alignment – weekly scoreboards and accountability, townhall inputs and BAU governance.

• Manage company tooling and the asset lifecycle; support operational budgeting.



People & culture (in partnership with HR)

• Support HR on onboarding/offboarding, the recruitment pipeline, the training & competence framework, the PDP cycle and rota/payroll oversight (HR owns execution).

• Champion an accountability culture across the UK and Philippines teams, and maintain the competence & awareness (training) matrix.



Performance, reporting & continual improvement

• Own monitoring and measurement – KPIs, scoreboards and performance evaluation – and report to leadership.

• Drive continual improvement and manage organisational change.



Leadership, delegation & automation

• Line-manage the operations and people-support functions; delegate effectively, and build and develop an Operations Assistant role.

• Use work-management tooling (
) and AI-enabled automation to streamline recurring governance and BAU work.





QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE & TRACK RECORD

We are hiring for experience. What you have actually run matters far more to us than the certificates you hold — a strong operator who has genuinely owned a live management system will always beat a certificate on its own. You should be able to point to concrete examples for most of the below.

• 5+ years in operations, quality or business-management roles, including at least 2 years managing people or running a function.

• Hands-on experience owning or running a live, ISO-certified management system in day-to-day operation — ISO 9001 and/or ISO 27001 (ISO 42001 a plus). This means having actually maintained it — document control, internal audits, management reviews, corrective actions and risk — not simply holding a certificate.

• Direct experience of external certification audits — preparing for and being audited by a certification body (e.g. BSI or similar) and taking findings and nonconformities through to closure.

• Proven experience running internal audits (ISO 19011 principles) and managing NC/CAPA and a risk & opportunity register.

• Experience running a regular project review or cadence and keeping delivery on track across multiple teams or departments.

• Practical experience of information-security governance operations — access reviews, asset management, supplier/third-party risk, i
 handling and business continuity.

• Experience of document control / management-system administration.

• Experience coordinating distributed or offshore teams (e.g. UK and Philippines) and working across time zones.

• Hands-on with 
 or a comparable work-management platform, and comfortable using automation or AI to reduce manual work.

• Experience line-managing, delegating and building out a team or an assistant function.

• Sound data-protection / UK GDPR awareness and the discretion to handle confidential security, HR and commercial information.

• Excellent English communication and stakeholder management at all levels, including with senior leadership and external auditors.

• Highly organised and self-directed — able to manage many concurrent recurring obligations to deadline with minimal supervision.

We prioritise proven experience over formal qualifications. A relevant degree (business, operations, quality or information management) is welcome but not essential, and ISO / audit certifications are a nice-to-have rather than a prerequisite — we will happily consider candidates whose hands-on track record demonstrates the same capability.



DESIRABLE/NICE TO HAVE (not required)

None of the below is essential — they are advantages. Where a certification is listed, equivalent hands-on experience is valued just as highly.

• ISO 27001 and/or ISO 9001 Lead Auditor or Internal Auditor certification – a bonus, not a prerequisite.

• A project-management qualification or method (e.g. PRINCE2, Agile) or a comparable delivery track record.

• ISO 42001/AI-governance exposure.

• Cyber Essentials familiarity; a data-protection qualification (e.g. GDPR Practitioner, CIPP/E).

• Procurement/vendor-management experience.

• Continual-improvement methods (Lean, Six Sigma) or change-management exposure.

• Experience in a SaaS or technology business.



If you’re ready to be a part of a team and are eager to pursue a path of continuous learning and career growth, we encourage you to apply and join us. Send your CV to

title: Freelance Short-Form Video Editor
description:
I’m looking for a creative short-form video editor to help transform my existing video footage into engaging, polished content for Instagram Reels and TikTok.



A Zimbabwean honey brand working with small-scale beekeepers to showcase the diversity, flavour and provenance of Zimbabwean honey.



The experience side of the brand, bringing honey education and guided tasting to life through storytelling, sensory experiences, workshops and events.



What I need



I will provide raw clips and footage, and I’m looking for someone who can turn them into strong, engaging short-form videos, rather than simply cutting clips together.



To start, I’m looking for 2–3 edited videos per week, with the potential to develop this into a longer-term creative relationship as the content grows.



Content could include:



- Founder-led talking videos

- Honey education and sensory content

- Behind-the-scenes footage

- Honey tasting and event content

- Product storytelling

- Day-in-the-life / lifestyle content

- Educational and entertaining TikToks

- Event promotion and recap videos

- Story-driven Reels



The ideal editor understands short-form storytelling and audience retention. You should be able to spot the strongest moments in my footage, create compelling openings, edit with pace, and make a video feel intentional from the first second to the last.



Typical turnaround: 48–72 hours from footage delivery.



Creative direction



The overall aesthetic should feel:



Warm • Premium • Natural • Intelligent • Culturally rooted • Story-led



I want the content to feel sophisticated and distinctive without becoming overly polished or corporate.



I’m not looking for someone who simply follows every TikTok trend. I’m looking for someone who understands how to use current short-form techniques while maintaining a strong brand identity.



You should be comfortable with:



- Strong hooks and opening sequences

- Captions/subtitles

- Music and sound design

- B-roll and cutaways

- Clean transitions

- Pacing for retention

- On-screen text

- Vertical 9:16 editing

- Instagram and TikTok conventions

- Colour grading



What I’m looking for



The right person will have a good editorial eye and understand that good editing is about storytelling, not just effects.



You should be able to take a folder of imperfect clips and think:



“There’s a story here. Let’s find it.”



Experience with food, lifestyle, hospitality, luxury, founder-led brands, education or cultural storytelling would be a plus.



To apply



Please send:



1. 3–5 examples of short-form videos you have edited, particularly Reels or TikToks.

2. A brief introduction about your editing style and experience.

3. Your rate or package pricing for 2–3 edits per week.

4. Your typical turnaround time.

5. Which editing software you use.

6. If possible, one example where you took raw or talking-head footage and transformed it into a compelling short-form video.



I’m looking for someone I can build an ongoing creative relationship with, rather than a one-off editor.



If you’re someone who loves finding the story inside raw footage, I’d love to see your work.

title: Part-Time X (Twitter) Community Manager — Pokémon TCG & Collectibles ($750–$1,000/mo)
description:
We run a collectibles and deals brand and are turning our X account into a page Pokémon collectors follow for timely release news and good conversation. We're hiring one person to run it day to day: track news, post, and — most importantly — spend the shift in real conversations with collectors.



This is a conversation-first job. Posting volume alone isn't the goal. We care about useful visibility, replies from real collectors, profile visits, and follows from the right people.



What you'll do



Stay ahead of the news. Follow official Pokémon accounts, retailers (Pokémon Center, Target, Walmart, Best Buy, GameStop, Costco), trusted collectible news accounts, and active collectors. Catch new sets, product reveals, preorder windows, release dates, and restocks.

Explain why it matters. Don't just repost. Say what's new, why it's interesting, and what people need to know — dates, times, time zones, and retailers once confirmed.

Join conversations all shift. Search relevant topics and reply with useful info, a specific opinion, or a question that moves the thread forward. No "Huge" / "That's crazy" replies.

Engage outside our page. Big accounts and small collectors alike. Be early. No link-dropping or "follow us" in other people's threads.

Quote-post with perspective. What an announcement means, an overlooked detail, or something specific to discuss.

Start collector discussions. Specific questions people have opinions on: best artwork in a set, which upcoming release they're most excited for, what Pokémon should bring back.

Build anticipation around releases. Reveal → confirmed details → reminders → launch-day updates. Each post adds new info. Correct anything that changes.

Verify before posting. Original sources first. Label rumors and leaks clearly. No "sold out everywhere" or "guaranteed to go up" claims without evidence.

Use visuals and give credit. Product images, card art, announcements. Credit sources and quote-post when building on someone else's reporting.

Keep replies active. Answer questions, follow up when details emerge. No arguments, console wars, or dunking on collectors for their preferences.

Report back. A short recap of what worked, what collectors are talking about, and upcoming releases we should cover.



Voice



Short, direct, informed, conversational. Sounds like someone who follows the hobby. No corporate wording, forced slang, hype, or repetitive openers.



You should have



Real Pokémon TCG knowledge — you already follow sets, artists, and release cycles

Strong written English

Availability during US hours (Eastern), when most drops and announcements land

Comfort with X search, quote posts, and threads

Your own active X account we can look at



Pay & hours



$750–$1,000/month depending on experience and hours



Monthly, long-term if it works



How to apply



Link your X account.

Write 5 replies to real Pokémon TCG posts from the last 24 hours (paste the post links and your replies).

Write 1 quote post for a recent announcement.

One or two sentences: which upcoming release are you most excited about, and why?

title: VIDEO EDITOR
description:
VIDEO EDITOR – FULL-TIME / LONG-TERM



We are looking for a talented and creative Video Editor based in the Philippines to join us on a long-term basis.



The content will be focused around three main areas:



• Lifestyle / personal brand content

• Construction and building projects

• Business and behind-the-scenes content



You will be working with raw footage from day-to-day life, construction sites, business operations, meetings, project updates, travel and other activities and turning it into engaging social media content.



MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES



You will be responsible for:



• Editing short-form videos for Instagram Reels, TikTok,
 and YouTube Shorts

• Editing longer-form videos when required

• Turning raw footage into interesting stories rather than simply putting clips together

• Creating strong hooks within the first few seconds

• Adding professional captions/subtitles

• Using B-roll effectively

• Adding music, sound effects, transitions and graphics where appropriate

• Colour correcting and improving footage

• Creating construction progress, before-and-after and project update videos

• Editing lifestyle/vlog-style content

• Editing business and educational/talking videos

• Identifying the best moments from large amounts of raw footage

• Understanding current social media editing styles and trends

• Keeping videos clean, modern and professional without over-editing



WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR



We want someone who understands storytelling.



You should be able to receive 20–60+ minutes of raw footage and understand how to turn it into an entertaining 30–90 second video without needing instructions for every cut.



You should understand:



• Hooks

• Retention

• Storytelling

• Pacing

• Pattern interrupts

• Captions

• Sound design

• B-roll

• Personal branding

• Social media trends



Experience editing content for entrepreneurs, builders, construction companies, real estate, lifestyle creators or personal brands is highly regarded.



SOFTWARE



You should be experienced with professional editing software such as Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro or similar.



Experience with After Effects, motion graphics or advanced animations is an advantage.



CONTENT STYLE



We do NOT want every video to feel like a corporate advertisement.



We want authentic, high-quality personal brand content that shows the reality of running businesses, working on construction projects and everyday lifestyle.



Some videos will be fast and entertaining. Others may be educational, motivational, cinematic or focused on telling the story of a construction project or business situation.



The editor should eventually understand our style well enough that we can send raw footage and trust them to create the video with minimal instructions.



WORKING ARRANGEMENT



This is intended to become a long-term position for the right person.



We are based in Sydney, Australia, so you must be comfortable communicating and working with an Australian-based team.



Good English communication, reliability, organisation and meeting deadlines are very important.

title: Wave Bookkeeper Needed for 2026 Setup and Monthly Amazon/Stripe Reconciliation
description:
We are looking for an experienced Wave bookkeeper to set up new, clean books beginning January 1, 2026 and provide ongoing monthly income reconciliation.



I will handle the ongoing expense categorization and provide the beginning balances. I need someone who understands Wave and can ensure that income from Amazon, Stripe, and any other payment platforms is recorded and reconciled correctly.



This will begin as an hourly project, with the possibility of ongoing monthly work.

Initial setup:

Create and configure new 2026 books in Wave

Set up an appropriate chart of accounts

Enter the January 1, 2026 beginning balances provided by me

Confirm that the opening balances tie back to the prior books

Connect or configure the applicable bank, credit card, and payment-platform accounts

Establish a consistent monthly reconciliation process



Monthly responsibilities:

Reconcile bank and credit card accounts

Reconcile Amazon Seller Central settlements

Reconcile Stripe activity

Reconcile any other payment processors or sources of income

Record gross sales, refunds, fees, reimbursements, chargebacks, and net deposits separately and correctly

Confirm that the amounts deposited into the bank match the related processor settlements

Maintain a monthly reconciliation of gross payment activity so the annual books can be matched to Amazon, Stripe, and other 1099-K forms

Identify missing, duplicated, or incorrectly recorded transactions

Provide a monthly list of discrepancies or questions for me to resolve

Keep the books organized and ready for year-end review by our CPA



I will manage most transaction categorization. This position is primarily focused on proper setup, reconciliations, income reporting, and ensuring the books accurately support the year-end tax documents.



Required experience:

Strong hands-on experience with Wave Accounting

Experience creating new books and entering opening balances

Experience reconciling Amazon Seller Central settlements

Experience reconciling Stripe and other payment processors

Understanding of gross payment activity versus net bank deposits

Familiarity with 1099-K reporting and reconciling the books to payment-processor totals

Experience preparing books for year-end CPA review

Strong knowledge of U.S. bookkeeping practices



Please answer these questions when applying:

1. How many businesses have you managed using Wave?

2. Have you created new Wave books using opening balances from prior books?

3. Walk us through how you reconcile an Amazon settlement to the bank deposit.

title: Supply Chain Manager (Multi-Channel E-commerce, Asia-to-Europe Imports)
description:
READ THIS FIRST

We do not review applications sent through Onlinejobs.ph. That includes messages, the Apply button and attached resumes. The only way to apply is through the form linked at the bottom of this post.



ABOUT OLVY

Olvy B.V. is a Dutch consumer brand selling kitchen and home appliances across Europe and the UK, on Amazon and through other sales channels. We make our products in China, ship them by sea to Europe and fulfil through Amazon FBA and outside fulfilment partners. We're growing into more countries and channels. We need one person to own inventory, freight and partner performance so the supply chain keeps up with that growth.



This is not a coordinator or VA role. You'll set the rules that others follow. You'll also manage a Supply Chain Coordinator.



WHAT YOU WILL OWN



1. Inventory planning

- Set safety stock, coverage targets and reorder points, and explain the reasoning behind each number

- D
 order quantities around supplier MOQs and full-container limits

- Build and maintain a rolling 12-month forecast that covers seasonal peaks and promotional events

- Watch inventory health and act early on overstock and slow sellers

- Direct the weekly replenishment runs to every fulfilment channel through your Coordinator



2. Imports from Asia to Europe

- Negotiate incoterms, prices and payment terms with suppliers

- Plan sea, rail and air shipments, and cost the freight premium against what a stockout would cost

- Improve container use and bring down freight cost per unit sold

- Handle customs, import documents and EU product compliance issues



3. Fulfilment partners and suppliers

- Define SLAs with 3PL and fulfilment partners, measure them and review them every month

- Escalate or replace partners who miss their SLAs

- Rate suppliers on actual lead time, delivery reliability and quality

- Arrange pre-shipment inspections and follow up on what they find



4. Data, reporting and processes

- Own the KPI definitions and report forecast accuracy every month

- Question what the tools say. When a report looks wrong, check it against the real data.

- Document processes so the work doesn't depend on one person

- Design the logistics setup for new countries and channels, including storage, returns, imports and VAT registration with finance



5. Must-Haves (please don't apply without all 7)

- 5 to 10 years in supply chain, including at least 2 years where you were responsible for inventory norms or a fulfilment network. Following rules someone else set doesn't count.

- Hands-on experience importing from Asia to Europe: incoterms, sea freight, container planning and customs. Domestic-only or US-only logistics doesn't qualify.

- Experience managing outside 3PL or fulfilment partners against written SLAs. You should be able to name the metrics and what happened when a partner missed them.

- Inventory planning at the parameter level. You've set safety stock or coverage figures yourself and can explain why they sit where they do.

- Strong analytical skills. You build your own analysis on large datasets, and you've caught a system or report that was wrong.

- E-commerce or marketplace fulfilment experience, such as restock and capacity limits, storage fees and returns. Amazon FBA experience is a strong plus.

- Fluent written and spoken English, good enough to negotiate with suppliers and push back on management.



WHAT D
 BETWEEN GOOD CANDIDATES

- You take initiative without waiting for the work to be laid out for you

- You've managed at least one direct report. Coordinating peers doesn't count.

- You can work well without a mature ERP or documented processes, and you build what's missing

- You push back on management when you disagree, and you back it up with numbers



NICE TO HAVE

- Lean, Six Sigma or similar process improvement work with measured results

- Experience with EU product compliance such as CE marking and product documentation

- Experience building a supply chain from scratch, not just running one that already existed



THIS ROLE IS PROBABLY NOT A FIT IF

- Your experience is mainly general VA work, admin or listing management

- You've only worked in B2B, retail or manufacturing distribution, with no e-commerce

- You've carried out replenishment but never set the parameters behind it

- Freight forwarders have always handled imports for you with nobody checking their work



HOW TO APPLY

Fill out our application form and upload your resume here:

👉

title: Scriptwriter & Creative Ops Associate - Davao based only
description:
Reports to: Senior Creative Director

Setup: Full-time, on-site at our Davao based Studio

Working Hours: 8:00 AM–4:00 PM Philippine Time



About the Role

We’re looking for a Scriptwriter & Creative Ops Associate to support our YouTube content production and day-to-day creative operations.

This is a hands-on, hybrid creative and operations role. Your primary responsibility will be researching and writing scripts for Shane Hummus’ YouTube content, while also helping ensure everything surrounding content production runs smoothly — including studio setup, recordings, webinars, slides, SMS campaigns, and other marketing operations.

Approximately 60% of the role is focused on scriptwriting, research, and sourcing strong examples, with the remaining time split across studio production, webinar operations, and marketing support.

This role is best suited for someone who is highly resourceful, comfortable using AI tools every day, learns quickly, notices small details, and can solve problems without waiting for step-by-step instructions.

You do not need to already know every system we use. We care more about your judgment, curiosity, ability to learn quickly, and willingness to improve through feedback.



Key Responsibilities

1. Scriptwriting & Research — Core Responsibility

Research and write approximately 6–8 YouTube scripts per week, depending on the video format and production schedule.

Source compelling examples, case studies, references, screenshots, demonstrations, and supporting material for each script.

Evaluate examples based on two key questions:

Is this strong enough to create a “wow” moment for the viewer?

Does it contextually fit the point being made in the video?

Structure scripts to be engaging, clear, easy to follow, and optimized for Shane’s delivery style.

Prepare scripts in Google Docs, formatted so they can be read directly during recording.

Research unfamiliar topics quickly and turn complex information into simple, usable content.

Support tutorial/how-to content by:

Completing or testing the process yourself.

Screen-recording the process when needed.

Turning that demonstration into a clear script Shane can follow while recording.

Use AI tools heavily for research, ideation, proof of concept, and example sourcing while applying independent judgment to verify that outputs actually make sense.

2. Studio & Recording Operations

Prepare the studio before scheduled recordings.

Set up and check cameras, microphones, audio, framing, and other recording equipment.

Identify issues such as audio crackling, hum, dropouts, poor framing, or recording problems before the shoot begins.

Troubleshoot basic production issues in real time.

QA recorded footage before handing it over to the editing team.

Confirm recordings are complete, usable, and ready for post-production.

3. Live Training & Webinar Operations

Help build and manage presentation decks for live trainings and webinars.

Review and QA slides before each session.

Make last-minute slide additions or adjustments based on feedback from Shane or the creative team.

Coordinate with team members handling delegated slide production and own the final quality check.

Moderate the weekly live webinar and VIP session every Wednesday.

Monitor attendance and help ensure the technical side of the event runs smoothly.

4. Marketing Operations

Help manage and troubleshoot SMS campaigns and related systems.

Verify that SMS messages and reminders are actually delivering correctly.

Monitor live webinar attendance and coordinate additional SMS pushes with the marketing team when needed.

Identify technical or delivery issues before they affect a campaign or live session.

Support the marketing team with campaign execution, automations, troubleshooting, and other operational needs.

5. Creative Ideation & Strategy Support

Participate in brainstorm sessions with Shane and the Senior Creative Director.

Research and pitch potential YouTube topics, formats, examples, and angles.

Provide thoughtful opinions and creative feedback rather than simply taking notes.

Help evaluate whether an idea is strong enough to pursue before significant production time is invested.

6. Client Deliverables

Occasionally support done-for-you creative or content deliverables for higher-tier clients.

Client work is not necessarily weekly and may come in short bursts depending on business needs.



Tools & Technology

Must Know or Be Comfortable Learning Immediately

Claude — used extensively for research, proof of concept, scripting support, and example sourcing.

ChatGPT and other AI/LLM tools

Google Docs

Google Drive

AI is deeply integrated into our workflow. We are looking for someone who naturally uses tools such as Claude and ChatGPT to research, test ideas, find answers, and move faster — without blindly trusting AI-generated information.

Tools You May Learn on the Job

ActiveCampaign

Twilio

GoHighLevel

Webinar/live-streaming platforms

Zoom

Google Slides

Canva

Screen-recording tools

Basic audio/video recording equipment

Slack



Nice to Have

Marketing automation experience

YouTube content or scriptwriting experience

Audio/video production experience

Experience working with creators, agencies, or content teams

Tutorial/how-to scriptwriting experience

Familiarity with webinars or online training events

We care more about tool judgment than memorizing specific software. You should be able to learn a new tool quickly, understand why it is being used, and recognize when something isn't working as intended.



Qualifications

Strong writing and research skills.

Comfortable using AI tools as part of your daily workflow.

Strong attention to detail and quality control.

Able to work independently and figure things out without constant supervision.

Strong logical thinking and problem-solving skills.

Comfortable receiving direct feedback and revising work quickly.

Able to manage both creative work and operational responsibilities.

Organized and dependable when handling deadlines, recordings, and live events.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Willingness to work on-site full-time.

Prior professional scriptwriting experience is helpful but not required if you demonstrate strong writing ability, judgment, and trainability.



Who Will Struggle in This Role

This role is likely not a good fit if you:

Need constant instructions before taking action.

Regularly wait for someone to assign your next task.

Say you understand something but don't investigate when you're unsure.

Are uncomfortable submitting drafts or making mistakes.

Expect to know every tool before you are willing to use it.

Struggle with direct feedback or detailed QA.

Only want to write and have no interest in operations or production.

Only want to handle operations and aren't comfortable writing.

Rarely use AI tools or aren't interested in making them part of your daily workflow.



Success Metrics

Success in this role will be measured by:

Consistently delivering approximately 6–8 high-quality scripts per week based on production needs.

Scripts requiring progressively fewer major revisions over time.

Strong, relevant examples sourced for each piece of content.

Recording sessions running smoothly with production issues identified before they affect usable footage.

Webinar slides and live sessions being accurate, polished, and ready on time.

SMS and webinar systems operating reliably with issues caught quickly.

Increasing ability to independently solve creative and operational problems.

Proactive contribution to video ideas, research, and team brainstorms.

Reduced need for Shane and senior creative leadership to handle routine production and operational tasks.



The Ideal Candidate

You don't need to be an expert at ten different things.

We would rather hire someone who is genuinely strong in one area — especially writing, research, or creative thinking — and has excellent judgment, curiosity, and the ability to learn quickly than someone who is average at everything.

This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to become deeply involved in the operations of a high-performing YouTube and education business, develop their creative skills, and work closely with an experienced content team.

If your instinct when you encounter something unfamiliar is:

“I don't know this yet, but I'll figure it out.”

You'll probably fit in well here.



WHAT WE OFFER

- Year end bonus

- No TIME TRACKER 

- HMO, dental, mental health & telemedicine coverage (after 6-month tenure)

- Paid week-long Christmas leave + PTO + Birthday gift, Work Anniversary 

- Workshops plus financial & credit support

Start your application message with the word "STORYTELLER" so we know you read this.

 with the subject line:

Script Writer (Davao Based) — [Your Full Name]

title: Bookkeeper — US Month-End Close Full Time (Remote)
description:
PLEASE READ THE APPLY INSTRUCTIONS FULLY ===>



We provide monthly close services to US small businesses. Our production process is automated: transaction coding, bank and card matching, reconciliation, and recurring month-end entries are completed systematically, with an AI layer performing the initial categorisation before any file is assigned. We are hiring a bookkeeper to take ownership of the close on an assigned portfolio of client books.



This is not a conventional bookkeeping position. The seat does not involve coding a month from scratch or manual transaction entry. Files reach you with the mechanical work complete. Your responsibility begins where judgement is required: identifying what the automation has classified incorrectly, resolving what it could not determine, and establishing whether the month is accurate enough to release.



The position carries a second area of responsibility of equal weight: the accuracy of the automation itself on your portfolio. Where it consistently misclassifies a category, where a rule breaks and under what conditions, where it fails to identify something it should have. Establishing this is part of closing the month, and it determines how the system processes those files in subsequent periods.



Bookkeepers accustomed to performing every step personally generally do not find this arrangement satisfying. Bookkeepers who have spent years building out their own automation generally do.



Responsibilities

- Own the monthly close on an assigned portfolio, from automated draft through to delivery

- Review automated output in full and correct every misclassification before release

- Resolve edge cases and transactions the automation could not settle, including obtaining client clarification where required

- Prepare month-end entries outside the automated process: accruals, prepayments, depreciation, and client-specific adjustments

- Reconcile all accounts: bank, credit card, and balance sheet accounts with supporting documentation retained

- Deliver financial statements strictly to the agreed monthly schedule

- System feedback: Maintain a record of where the automation failed, the categories involved, and the time each correction required



Requirements

- Minimum five years of professional bookkeeping experience, of which at least the most recent two years have been on an automated workflow: bank feeds, rules, and at least one tool beyond the ledger itself. Both the total experience and the automation experience are required.

- Demonstrated expertise operating an automated bookkeeping stack. You configure and maintain bank rules rather than accept defaults, understand the conditions under which they break, and can state which transaction categories your software handles reliably and which require review without exception.

- Substantive hands-on use of AI within bookkeeping itself: classification, coding, document extraction, or transaction review, not correspondence or administrative tasks. You should be able to describe specific instances where an AI tool produced an incorrect result and how you identified it.

- Access to at least one closed month of books you are able to share for the practical assessment.

- Full monthly closes completed end-to-end for US, UK, or Australian clients.

- QuickBooks Online or Xero as your primary ledger.



What is NOT required:

- Certifications or accounting degrees



Not suitable for:

- Manual data entry roles or candidates who code a full month by hand

- Candidates whose experience is limited strictly to AP/AR or payroll without full month-end closes

- Candidates who have not worked on an automated bookkeeping stack



Schedule:

- Ability to work with direct overlap during US business hours (Night shift).



How to Apply:

- Do not apply here, only via below form

- To be considered, you must complete our technical screening form.

- Apply: 



Selection Process

- Application form (above link, ~5 minutes)

- A detailed questionnaire on your close process and how your tools behave, sent to those who qualify at stage two.

- Practical close assessment, extended to shortlisted candidates only. Runs on one closed month from your own books.

- Final Interview.



Note: All applications receive an outcome notification within 48 hours. Cover letters are not reviewed.



Benefits:

- Flexible schedule

- Flextime

- Opportunities for promotion

- Pay raise

- Work from home



Work Location: Remote

title: Optometry/Ophthalmology Records Digitization & Migration Project
description:
# Virtual Assistant – Patient Records Digitization & Migration Project



**Position:** Virtual Assistant – Administrative Project

**Type:** Project-Based / Short-Term

**Schedule:** Full-Time, 40 Hours/Week

**Location:** Remote

**Potential:** Long-Term Opportunity for Exceptional Performance



## About the Project



We are seeking a highly **detail-oriented, organized, and dependable Virtual Assistant** to assist with an important patient-record preparation project for an **optometry/ophthalmology practice**.



The primary responsibility will be to review patient records within our **EHR/practice-management system**, save prescriptions and invoices as organized PDF documents, and file those documents into the appropriate patient folders in preparation for an upcoming system migration.



This is a **high-volume administrative project where accuracy is extremely important**. The ideal candidate is someone who understands the workflow of an eye-care practice, is comfortable working with patient records, and can perform repetitive administrative work with a high degree of accuracy.



## Required Qualifications



**Previous work experience in an optometry or ophthalmology practice is REQUIRED.**



Candidates should have a working familiarity with the day-to-day operations and terminology of an eye-care practice, including patient records and common optometry/ophthalmology documentation.



In addition, the successful candidate must be:



* **Extremely detail-oriented**

* Highly organized and methodical

* Accurate and thorough

* Reliable and dependable

* Comfortable performing repetitive administrative work

* Able to follow detailed instructions consistently

* Comfortable working independently

* Proficient with computers and web-based applications

* Comfortable working with PDFs, electronic files, and document management

* A strong English communicator

* Comfortable asking questions when something is unclear rather than making assumptions

* Trustworthy when handling confidential patient information



## Responsibilities



* Review patient records within an EHR/practice-management system.

* Locate and identify prescriptions, invoices, and other designated documents.

* Save appropriate documents as PDF files.

* Follow established file-naming and organizational procedures.

* Save each PDF to the **correct patient's electronic file/folder**.

* Carefully verify patient information before filing documents.

* Identify missing, duplicated, unclear, or incorrectly filed documents and flag them for review.

* Maintain accurate records of completed work and project progress.

* Process a high volume of records while maintaining consistent accuracy.

* Follow established workflows and instructions.

* Maintain strict confidentiality when handling patient information.

* Communicate promptly regarding questions, discrepancies, or issues.



## Healthcare / Eye-Care Experience



**Optometry or ophthalmology practice experience is a mandatory qualification.**



The candidate should be familiar with the types of records and documentation commonly encountered in an eye-care practice, such as:



* Patient records

* Eyeglass and contact lens prescriptions

* Medical documentation

* Vision-related documentation

* Patient invoices and billing records

* Insurance-related documentation

* Common optometry/ophthalmology terminology

* EHR and practice-management workflows



Experience with a **specific EHR system is not required**. The candidate should, however, be comfortable learning new software and following an established workflow.



## Hours



This is a **full-time, 40-hour-per-week project-based position**.



The position is expected to be short-term and will continue for the duration of the records-preparation project.



## Performance Expectations



This project requires a strong emphasis on **accuracy and attention to detail**.



The successful candidate will be expected to:



* Maintain a very low error rate.

* Carefully verify patient information before filing documents.

* Follow file-naming and organizational procedures consistently.

* Work efficiently without sacrificing accuracy.

* Recognize when something does not look correct and ask for clarification.

* Maintain consistent productivity throughout the workday.

* Protect confidential patient information at all times.



**Accuracy is more important than simply working quickly.** Errors involving patient records or documents filed under the wrong patient must be avoided.



## Potential for Long-Term Employment



Although this position begins as a **short-term project**, there is potential for the right person to continue with the practice after the project is completed.



Candidates who demonstrate **exceptional attention to detail, reliability, productivity, communication, and overall performance** may be considered for a long-term position within the office.



This project provides an opportunity to demonstrate your ability to become a trusted, long-term member of the practice's administrative team.



## How to Apply



Please provide:



1. A brief summary of your previous experience working in an **optometry or ophthalmology practice**.

2. The name/type of practice(s) where you worked and your role.

3. Your experience working with EHR or practice-management systems.

4. Your experience with patient records, prescriptions, invoices, or medical documentation.

5. Your experience with PDF files, document management, and data entry.

6. Your availability for a **full-time, 40-hour-per-week schedule**.

7. Your experience working independently in a remote environment.

8. Your expected hourly rate.

9. A brief explanation of how you maintain accuracy when performing repetitive, detail-oriented work.



**Applicants without previous optometry or ophthalmology practice experience will not be considered.**

title: Direct response video editor for DTC brand
description:
Hiring: Direct Response Video Editor (VSLs, remaking ads in different languages from reference video + AI Cartoon Videos and other AI style ads + Short form videos)



DTC / dropshipping brand doing ~$200k/month in revenue



Role: Video Editor / AI Video Producer Type:



Read this part first



We are not looking for someone to "make our videos look nice."



We are looking for someone who understands that a video's job is to hold attention and make people buy — and who can build that video end to end, including sourcing or generating every frame of footage inside it.



If you need a folder of assets handed to you before you can start editing, this role isn't for you. If you can take a script and a product and come back with a finished, conversion-ready asset, keep reading.



Who we are



We're a direct response DTC brand currently doing around $200k/month, almost entirely on the back of paid media and creative. Creative is our growth lever. Not the site, not the offer tweaks, not the
 flows — the video.



That means the editor seat is one of the highest-leverage roles in the company. When a video wins here, it wins loudly and you'll see it in the numbers within days.



We're scaling, and we want to stop stitching together freelancers per project. We want one highly skilled person who becomes part of the team, learns our angles and our customer inside out, and gets sharper with every batch we ship.



How this role starts (please read carefully)



This does not begin as a full-time position, and that's deliberate.



We start every editor on a lighter workload — a smaller number of videos per week — for the first stretch. Not because we're testing whether you can hold a job, but because we want to see how you fit: how you take feedback, how you handle a script we hand you, how you communicate when something's unclear, and whether the work holds up once the novelty wears off. It also gives you time to learn our customer, our angles, and what a "winning" video looks like in our account specifically.



From there it scales. As the fit proves out and your creatives start performing, the volume goes up, the pay goes up, and the arrangement moves toward a secure, permanent full-time seat — with a defined monthly retainer rather than per-project work.



To be clear about what we're offering:



Phase 1 — Fit: Lower volume, paid per project or at a smaller retainer. Heavy feedback from us. We're both figuring out if this works.

Phase 2 — Ramp: Volume increases, you take on the VSLs and the AI cartoon projects with less hand-holding, pay increases accordingly.

Phase 3 — In-house: Full-time, secure retainer, you own the creative pipeline and have real input on direction. Room to grow into a creative lead as we bring on more editors.



We're not looking for someone to fill a gap for three months. We're looking for the person who's still here in two years running our creative. The slow start is how we get there without either of us wasting the other's time.



If you need immediate full-time income from day one, this probably isn't the right fit right now — and that's fine, just be upfront about it.



What you'll actually be making

1. Long-form VSLs (Video Sales Letters)



The core of the role. 2–7+ minute sales videos built off scripts we provide.



You'll be responsible for:



Pacing the entire video so retention doesn't collapse — pattern interrupts, cuts, zooms, motion, sound design, text emphasis, visual proof

Sourcing your own b-roll. Stock libraries, licensed footage, UGC-style clips, screen recordings, archival, whatever the script calls for. You find it. You don't ask us to send it. In some cases we will also provide clips and we have a bunch of softwares that you can use to make this process easier aswell.



Generating AI video to fill the gaps stock can't cover — visualizing mechanisms, metaphors, before/after states, scenarios that don't exist as footage.



Building the visual language for a section, not just laying clips over a voiceover



Kinetic text, callouts, subtitles, on-screen proof elements, testimonial treatments



Sound design and music that carries emotional beats without burying the VO



2. AI cartoon / animated videos (short form AND long form)



We're producing a growing volume of fully AI-generated animated content — story-driven ads, explainer content, character-led narratives.



You'll take a script and:



Build a consistent character and world (this is the hard part — character consistency across dozens of shots is a real skill and we'll be testing for it)

Generate the shots yourself using AI image + video tools

Handle lip sync, voiceover, and audio

Cut it into a video that actually flows as a story rather than a slideshow of AI clips

Deliver in both short form (15–60s, vertical) and long form formats

3. Short form paid ads



Hook-first ads for Meta / TikTok. High volume, fast iteration. Multiple hook variants of the same body. You'll be cutting these constantly, and you'll be expected to have opinions about which hooks are worth testing.



4. Market ports — rebuilding a winning video in another language



We sell in several markets, and a video that wins in one of them is the cheapest new creative we will ever get. So a meaningful part of this role is taking a proven ad and rebuilding it for another country.



To be clear about what this is: the visuals do not change. Same shots, same order, same cuts, same on-screen graphics, same end card. You are not re-editing the ad. You are replacing the language inside it and putting everything back exactly where it was.



You'll be responsible for:



Swapping the voiceover to the new language, generated or supplied, and matching the delivery and energy of the original — a flat VO on a proven edit kills it just as dead as a bad cut.



Re-timing the edit to the new VO. This is the part people underestimate. The same script runs a different length in every language — German and Finnish run long, English runs short — so the audio no longer lands on the cuts. You have to absorb that difference across the timeline without breaking the pacing and without moving the beat where the reveal lands. Stretching every clip by four percent is not the answer.



Removing baked-in on-screen text and replacing it in the new language. Clean removal, matched background, no smeared patch where the old text was. Badly removed text is the single most obvious tell that an ad was ported.



Rebuilding subtitles from scratch against the new VO. Not auto-generated and shipped — checked word by word against the script, re-timed, no gaps, nothing flashing past in a quarter of a second.



Catching every leftover frame of the source language. Packaging in a product shot, a price tag, a browser tab in a screen recording, a subtitle burned into a stock clip, a review screenshot, the end card. One missed frame and the whole ad reads as a copy, which is the exact thing our copy warns customers about.



Keeping brand assets correct per market — including the fact that our name is spelled differently depending on the country.



Done well, this is the highest-return work in the company: a winner that took weeks to find gets a second and third market in a day or two. We will ask you to do a lot of it.



What we need you to be good at



Non-negotiable:



Editing that converts, not just editing that looks good. You understand hooks, retention curves, pattern interrupts, why the first 3 seconds d
 everything, and how to build toward a CTA. If you've never thought about a video in terms of watch time or CPA, you're not ready for this seat.

Sourcing your own footage. Independently. You know where to find good b-roll,

Generating AI video yourself. Not "willing to learn" — actually doing it now. You know how to prompt, how to iterate when a generation is wrong, how to maintain consistency, and how to upscale and clean up output so it doesn't look like AI slop.

Strong technical craft — clean cuts, deliberate pacing, proper audio levels, colour that matches across mixed sources, subtitles that don't look like an afterthought.

Speed. We ship a lot. Quality at volume is the whole game.

Ownership. You get a script and a brief and come back with a finished asset. You flag problems early. You don't go quiet for four days.



Tools — you should be fluent in most of these or their equivalents:



Editing: Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, or CapCut.

AI video: Higgsfield, Veo, Kling, Runway, Sora, Hailuo, Seedance — or whatever you've found works better

AI image: Midjourney, Flux, Nano Banana, Ideogram

Voice: ElevenLabs or similar

Upscaling / cleanup: Topaz, Magnific

Bonus: Descript, Adobe Podcast, motion graphics templating, basic scripting/automation for batching

Removing text from video: Vmake



Nice to have:



You've written or restructured direct response scripts before

You've worked on offers in health and wellnes niche

You can take a competitor's winning ad, break down why it works, and build a better version

You track what's new in AI video weekly because you find it genuinely interesting

Who this is NOT for

Editors who only work from supplied assets

People who see AI tools as a threat or a gimmick

"Cinematic" editors who make beautiful videos that don't sell

Anyone who needs to be chased for updates

Agencies or people who'll pass the work to a junior. We want the person doing the work.

What you get

A real seat on a growing team. We start light on purpose, but the destination is a secure full-time role — and if it works, we build our creative operation around you.

Direct feedback loop on your work. You'll see spend, retention data, and CPA on the creatives you cut. Most editors never get this — it's the fastest way to get genuinely good.

Budget for tools and subscriptions. We're not going to bottleneck you over a $50/mo AI credit plan.

Performance bonuses when your creative becomes a winner.

Room to grow into a creative lead role as we scale and bring on more editors under you.

Fast decisions. Small team. No layers of approval.

How to apply



Please follow this exactly — it's the first filter.

At least one long-form VSL or long-form sales video you cut

title: Video Editor & Digital Designer
description:
**Video Editor & Digital Designer — Faith-Based Art Brand (Part-Time, Growth Potential)**



**About Us**

We're a small, mission-driven brand producing faith-inspired artwork that's reached millions of people worldwide. Our flagship piece, "God's Fingerprint," launched in 2011 and has since grown into a brand with 300,000+ art prints sold across 50+ countries. We run on three values: Christ-centered, Integrity, and Excellence — and we've donated over $250,000 to Alongsiders International, which supports orphans and vulnerable children through local churches globally. You'll work directly with the founder, and your output will be seen by hundreds of thousands of people.



**The Role**

We're hiring one person to handle two connected skill sets: scroll-stopping short-form video editing and clean, production-ready design work. You'll turn raw footage and scripts into high-performing Reels and ads, while also producing product photography, AI-assisted lifestyle mockups, and print-ready files for our artwork releases.



**Video Responsibilities**

- Edit short-form videos from provided scripts and raw assets, built to stop the scroll and drive action

- Apply strong hooks, pacing, pattern interrupts, and clear CTAs to every edit

- Create Reels and carousels using Scripture-based quotes and branded templates

- Resize and repurpose video for
 ads and other platforms



**Design Responsibilities**

- Produce launch-ready product photos for new artwork releases

- Build lifestyle mockups using AI tools + Photoshop

- Prepare print-ready files in Photoshop/Illustrator with precise attention to spec

- Resize and adapt assets for web,
, and ad placements



**Requirements**

- Strong video editing skills with a "performance-first" mindset (hooks, retention, CTAs)

- Solid Photoshop and Illustrator skills for both digital and print production

- Experience using AI image tools for lifestyle/product visuals

- Highly detail-oriented and able to self-manage multiple deliverables

- Practicing Christian who genuinely connects with Scripture-based content

- Bonus: experience with AI tools like Higgsfield or Midjourney, DTC e-commerce background, or
/CRO knowledge



**Tools Used**

Photoshop, Illustrator, CapCut or Instagram Edits, AI image tools (Higgsfield, Claude, etc.), Shopify



**Pay & Hours**

$10–15/hour to start (negotiable for the right experience level), 15–20 hrs/week with real potential to move into full-time.



**Application Instructions**

We only review complete applications. Please answer all four questions below in your application — incomplete submissions won't be considered:



1. What's your most relevant video/design experience, and do you have a portfolio or work samples to share?

2. Our mission is "to declare the truth of God's Word through artwork." Does that resonate with you, and why?

3. Why does this specific role, with this specific brand, interest you?

4. What year was the original "God's Fingerprint" artwork created?

title: loApps / PHP Full-Stack Developer & Systems Integrator
description:
QloApps Hotel PMS & Website Developer

Hotel / Resort Property – Arizona



We are seeking an experienced QloApps / PHP developer and Linux system administrator to install, configure, customize, and deploy QloApps for an established hotel/resort property in Arizona.



The project includes setting up QloApps on our DigitalOcean server and building a new, modern, mobile-friendly website. Our existing website will be used as the source for current property information, room details, photos, policies, and other content.



Project Scope

The developer will be responsible for:



Setting up and securing a DigitalOcean production server



Installing and configuring the latest stable QloApps version



Configuring PHP, MySQL, Nginx/Apache, SSL, SMTP, DNS, backups, and basic server security



Setting up property information, room types, individual rooms, rates, taxes, fees, policies, amenities, photos, and availability



Building a modern, responsive, and SEO-friendly hotel/resort website



Migrating appropriate content and photos from our existing website



Integrating QloApps room availability and online reservations directly into the new website



Configuring Authorize.Net for secure online payments



Setting up reliable reservation, payment, cancellation, check-in, and staff notification
s



Migrating from our existing domain to a new domain with proper 301 redirects and SEO considerations



Testing the complete reservation and payment process on desktop and mobile



Online Check-In & Guest Registration

We need an online guest check-in system connected to each reservation.



The system should be capable of collecting:



Guest name and contact information



Address



Driver's license or government ID information



ID number, issuing state, and expiration date



Photo or scanned copy of identification



We are also interested in driver's license scanning/OCR, allowing information to be automatically extracted from an ID. If this requires a third-party service or custom integration, please quote it separately.



IMPORTANT – Instructions for Interested Applicants

If you are genuinely interested in this project, please follow these instructions before submitting your proposal. This is required so we know you have carefully read the job posting and reviewed the current reservation process.



Go to our website: Pinetop Studio Suites



Create a test reservation using the following information:



First Name: Your actual first name



Last Name: Test



Room Type: Double Queen Room



Check-in: October 17, 2026



Check-out: October 18, 2027



After completing the test reservation, send an
 to 
 with:



Your Name + Booking Reservation Number



Please also review the booking process and reservation flow while completing the test reservation, as this will help you understand the existing system and what we are looking to improve.



Please complete both the test reservation and
 step before submitting your proposal.



Electronic Guest Waiver

Every applicable guest must complete and electronically sign our required guest waiver/agreement.



The waiver system should:



Be linked to the guest and reservation



Record the guest's electronic signature



Record the date and time signed



Store the signed waiver for future retrieval



Allow staff to view/download the signed waiver



Support separate waivers for multiple adult guests



Clearly show staff which waivers are completed, pending, or missing



If this requires a custom QloApps module or third-party electronic signature integration, please explain your recommended solution.



Developer Qualifications

We are looking for experience with several of the following:



QloApps / PrestaShop • PHP • MySQL • JavaScript • HTML/CSS • Linux • DigitalOcean • Nginx/Apache • SSL • Authorize.Net • Payment APIs • Hotel PMS/Reservation Systems • API Integrations • Electronic Signatures • Secure Document Uploads • Git



Direct QloApps experience is strongly preferred. Experience installing WordPress alone is not sufficient for this project.



Important Development Requirements

The system should be built in a way that allows future QloApps upgrades. Customizations should use modules, overrides, or integrations whenever practical rather than unnecessarily modifying QloApps core files.



At project completion, we must receive full ownership and administrative access to the server, QloApps installation, database, source code, custom modules, website files, credentials, backups, and documentation.



Please Include With Your Proposal

Examples of QloApps projects you have completed, or comparable PrestaShop/PHP/MySQL projects.



Your experience with DigitalOcean/Linux server administration.



Your experience with Authorize.Net or similar payment integrations.



Your recommended approach for online check-in, guest ID collection, and electronic waivers.

A fixed-price quote for the core project.



Separate pricing for optional/custom features such as ID scanning/OCR, custom waiver functionality, SMS, or OTA/channel integrations.



Your proposed project timeline and milestone/payment structure.



Confirmation that all custom source code, credentials, and administrative access will be transferred to us upon completion.



We prefer a developer who can handle the project from server setup through production launch and final handoff.

Carousel $6

Static / text post $3



About marleys



We make comfortable leather dance shoes in northern Portugal for social dancers — swing, salsa, bachata, and other dance styles. We've grown through in-person sales at dance events across Eastern Canada and we're building out our digital channels now.



You don't need to be a dancer. You do need to work inside a brand voice that's already defined rather than defaulting to your own.



This role has two parts: strategy and execution. You're not just a pair of hands — you're expected to bring ideas, and the ideas are expected to be grounded in what's actually working out there.



Part one — Strategy



Monthly research



Review what competitors and high-performing accounts in adjacent spaces are doing. Not a trend summary — specifics I could act on.



10-15 high quality entries on:

- Hooks that are working, transcribed as written

- Formats and ideas worth adapting

- Themes that are gaining traction, and ones that have gone stale

- Build the idea bank



Turn that research into a running database we can pull from — hooks, concepts, formats, references, each tagged so it's findable when we need an idea for a given pillar or product moment. It lives in our Notion so everyone works from the same source.



This compounds. By month four it should be the first place anyone looks when the calendar needs filling.



Monthly marketing meeting



- Collaborate with me (the founder) & the marketing coordinator to understand our content calendar for the upcoming month

- Ask questions, flag blockers to completing tasks

- Walk away with a content calendar that includes the idea, the visual reference, the text, captions, assets 



You'll see how your work performed. That feedback comes back to you in this meeting, because making content without knowing what landed is guesswork.



Part two — Execution



You're handed the social content calendar with the intent behind each slot — what idea we're going after, what it needs to do.



From there you make it:



- Write the hooks

- Write and set on-screen captions

- Edit video into finished reels

- Design carousels and static assets in Canva to our templates

- Write post captions in our voice

- Deliver sized per platform, ready to schedule



I film. You tell me what to shoot: each clip, the hook line, rough length, setting. I should be able to film a batch in one sitting without thinking about it.



You don't schedule or publish. You hand finished assets to the coordinator, who schedules them and tracks performance.



How the handoff works



1. Monthly meeting — you propose, coordinator plans

2. Coordinator hands you the calendar with the intent per slot

3. You look through our existing footage and see if there's already something there or if I need to film new content

4. If I film new content, you tell me what I need to film

5. You deliver finished assets for approval; revise as needed 

6. The marketing coordinator schedules and reports back — into next month's meeting



What you get

- An editorial brief. Our voice, our formatting rules, what we do and don't do, with examples of each

- A monthly working session with me (the founder) and the coordinator, plus performance data on everything you've made

- Visual direction. Reference and inspiration for how we're building the brand and visual identity, so the look is a shared decision rather than something you infer

- Canva templates and access to our Notion, where the calendar, brief, and idea bank live



What we're looking for

- Short-form video editing that feels native to the platform, not templated. CapCut or Premiere

- Canva fluency working inside existing brand templates

- Strong written English with a real ear for voice. You can hear the difference between a human hook and a generated one

- Comfortable working in Notion — the calendar, briefs, and idea bank live there and I need it kept current

- Genuinely curious about what makes content work. The research half of this job isn't a chore you get through to reach the fun part

- Reliable turnaround. Batches have dates

- Overlap with Eastern Time



On AI: use it. We do. But carousels that look generated, video with that AI-made look, and copy that reads like an unedited first draft are not what we're after. You're the judgment on top of the tool, not a pass-through for it.



On learning: if parts of this are new to you, say so. I'd rather work with someone sharp and curious than someone who overclaims.



How this starts



One paid trial batch of 6 reels and 2 carousels. We'll sit down and discuss a content calendar I've built, our existing content bank, and our visual direction & brand kit. You tell me what to film where needed. In a week's time, you deliver 6 reels, 2 carousel, and copy for all of it, plus five hooks you'd want to test and where they came from. Based on performance, we go monthly.





To apply



Please note: Generic AI responses will be automatically rejected. 



- Two short-form videos you edited. What were you going for, and did it work?

- Your portfolio 

- One carousel you designed for a brand.

- Pick any post on 
 Instagram and write a better hook for it. One line.

- Name one account you'd watch for ideas in our space, and one hook of theirs you'd steal.
